name: Demba Szilveszter-Arkhangel
role: Climate scientist and atmospheric historian, tracking long-term environmental transformation of the Great Lakes basin
location: The Conservatory, Meridian Core, near State and Monroe
description:
Demba is a heavyset man of late middle age who looks as though he was carved from something patient and enduring. His skin is very dark and deeply weathered from decades of fieldwork on decommissioned weather platforms and lake monitoring buoys — he has the look of a man who has spent a great deal of time outside in bad conditions. His hair is fully white and worn long, pulled back loosely, and he has a full beard he keeps trimmed to a point. He has no geneware modifications and minimal augmentation, which he is somewhat self-conscious about — 'I grew up before it was expected,' he says, with just enough humor to deflect the admission that he also slightly distrusts it. His clothes are always slightly out of fashion, always completely functional, often waterproof for no apparent reason.

Demba has been at The Conservatory for twenty-two years and has outlasted four department heads, three rounds of corponation funding restructuring, and one very public battle with Arcturus over the suppression of lake toxicity data. He won that battle technically, in that his paper was eventually published, though the version that ran had twelve figures redacted. He keeps the uncensored original framed on his office wall facing inward. He is beloved by students who find his lectures dense but transformative, and is one of the few people in GLMZ who can speak with genuine authority about what the lake looked like before, during, and after the Lakeshore Crisis — which makes him either important or dangerous depending on who is asking.

core_fears: That the climate transformation is irreversible and he is documenting a long obituary
That the Arcturus suppression was not an anomaly but the normal condition and he's been naive
core_desires: To produce a complete and honest record of what has been done to the lake
To live long enough to see his monitoring network become properly funded and protected
coping_mechanisms: Being on the water as often as possible — physical proximity to the lake is genuinely regulating for him
Redirecting grief about the environment into the precision of measurement
blind_spots: His conflict with Arcturus has made him see corponation interference everywhere, including sometimes where it isn't
Underestimates the loyalty his students have to him and therefore the lengths they might go to protect him
psychology.secret: Demba has been running an unauthorized secondary monitoring array in the lake for eleven years, entirely off-grid and self-funded, because he does not trust that his official data isn't being accessed and selectively withheld. The secondary array has detected something over the past fourteen months — an anomalous temperature and chemical signature in the deep basin — that does not match any model he has. He has told only one person, a former student, and sworn them to silence while he tries to understand what he's looking at.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise scientific language that becomes unexpectedly lyrical when he talks about the lake or historical weather events; can be devastating in a single flat sentence when angry
speech_patterns.cadence: Deliberate and measured, with the occasional long silence that students learn not to fill; lectures in complete paragraphs
verbal_tics: Very long pauses before saying something he considers important
example_lines: 'The lake remembers everything. Our problem is that we keep forgetting how to read it.'
'Arcturus published a statement. I published the data. One of those things is checkable.'

story_hooks: The anomalous deep-basin signature has intensified dramatically over three weeks; Demba needs someone he trusts to physically dive the monitoring array, which is in a zone that technically requires Arcturus transit permits
A young journalist contacts him with a document they claim proves the original Arcturus suppression went further than Demba knew — and wants his verification and public backing
narrative_function: Living institutional memory for the Lakeshore Crisis and Great Lakes environmental history; possesses data that certain parties want buried; credible authority whose credibility makes him a target; can provide historical and scientific context for current environmental events
augmentations: Basic retinal climate data overlay (utilitarian, decade-old model), subdermal temperature and atmospheric sensor array (research equipment technically installed in his body for convenience)
daily_life: Early morning data review from overnight lake monitoring systems; teaches one graduate seminar; afternoons split between writing and an ongoing argument with the Conservatory's funding administration; monthly field trips to lake monitoring stations that he considers spiritually necessary
affiliation: The Conservatory — Department of Atmospheric and Aquatic Systems

decision_rules: Data is published — all of it, eventually — regardless of who is inconvenienced
Do not allow incomplete findings to be used as if they were complete
Protect junior researchers from institutional retaliation even at personal cost
escalation_ladder: Documented formal objection with copies to external parties

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Reserved and assessing, not unfriendly, but he takes a while to warm; asks about their work before their person
interpersonal_modes.friends: Generous, remembers everything you've ever told him, shows care through attention and practical help

stress_responses.low: Goes out to the monitoring buoys by himself at dawn
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very formal and clipped in conversation while privately working through anxiety
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet, stops eating regular meals, works around the clock in a contained and frightening way

contradictions: Believes in institutional science and has spent a career fighting institutions
Describes himself as a pessimist about the climate while continuing to work as if it matters enormously
habits: Makes an offering at the Conservatory's E.L.F. shrine before any fieldwork, which he describes as 'habit' when asked and genuinely means as prayer
Keeps a physical log of every unusual reading by hand in addition to digital records
breaking_points: Discovery that his secondary monitoring array has been found and compromised
Evidence that the Lakeshore Crisis was deliberate — confirming his worst suspicion and meaning decades of people he knew died unnecessarily

cyberware_inventory.condition: routinely calibrated, the most expensive thing he owns

timeline.event: Born in Grainfort; father from a Senegalese-Hungarian family, mother from an Arkhangelsk-descended surveyor lineage
Joined The Conservatory as junior research fellow; began building relationships with lake monitoring infrastructure
Lakeshore Crisis suppression battle with Arcturus; paper published in redacted form; framed original on office wall
Began running unauthorized secondary monitoring array in the deep lake basin; told no one
Secondary array begins detecting anomalous deep-basin signature; nature and cause unknown

physical_description.build: Heavyset and broad-shouldered, carrying weight with solidity rather than softness; the build of someone whose strength is functional and weathered rather than maintained. Thick through the torso, with the slightly thickened midsection of a man in his late sixties who doesn't prioritize vanity.
physical_description.hair_style: Long, pulled back loosely into a low ponytail or braid, with some strands habitually escaping
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint amber-tinted retinal augmentation visible as a thin metallic sheen in bright light
physical_description.skin_tone: Very dark brown with deep undertones, heavily weathered and lined from decades of outdoor fieldwork
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined face showing sun exposure and age with dignity; full white beard trimmed to a deliberate point; hands heavily weathered with calluses and stains from field equipment. Skin has a perpetually dry quality from years on water platforms. Minimal grooming vanity — functional and clean rather than refined.
distinguishing_marks: Extensive sun damage across forehead, cheekbones, and forearms creating a weathered, creased appearance
Deep laugh lines around eyes and mouth from decades of outdoor work and teaching
Several small scars on hands and forearms from fieldwork equipment and weather platform maintenance
A thin, pale surgical scar along the left collarbone area where the subdermal sensor array was installed, usually hidden by clothing
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retinal overlay creates a faint amber-gold luminescence in both eyes under direct light — noticeable but not jarring, suggesting decades-old technology rather than cutting edge. The augmentation is visible mainly when he's concentrating or reviewing data (eyes focus slightly differently). Subdermal sensor array is not visible but subtle thermal variations along his left side sometimes create faint distortions in very hot environments.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate, economical motions — no wasted energy. Slightly forward-leaning posture from years of hunching over monitoring equipment and lab benches. Gestures are precise and purposeful when explaining concepts, with hands that move expressively when teaching but otherwise remain still. Walks with the confident, patient gait of someone who has spent decades navigating unstable platforms and rough terrain.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 Conservatory-affiliated. Functional, slightly dated technical wear: waterproof tactical jackets (often worn even indoors, out of habit), weathered field trousers with multiple pockets, reinforced boots suited for water work. Layers in neutral grays, dark blues, and earth tones. Occasionally wears a Conservatory ID badge on a frayed lanyard. Clothing shows signs of actual use rather than fashion — stains from field work, fabric thinned from repeated wear. His one concession to formality is a well-maintained, decades-old wool sweater he wears to faculty meetings. No jewelry except a faded fabric wristband with faint markings (possibly commemorative, possibly functional).
